## Natural history notes

A small emerald moth characterized by pale green wings crossed by fine whitish lines and often edged or accented with reddish to pinkish margins that give it the “red-bordered” appearance. In Florida, the Red-bordered Emerald is found in wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, pine flatwoods, parks, and yards where suitable shrubs and trees occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on woody plant foliage and help transfer leaf growth into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
